land.text: the Chengdu Plain, where Shu appears in 1046

successors.note: Many Chinese archaeologists identify Sanxingdui with Shu; the pages leave a gap between c. 1150 (end of Sanxingdui) and 1046 (Shu at Muye), bridged by Jinsha (Shi'erqiao culture 1200-800).

capitals.name: Sanxingdui walled city (Guanghan)
capitals.note: 'A walled city founded c. 1,600 BCE' of 3.6 km2 about 4 km northeast of Nanxing Township; coordinates are the researcher's. Whether it was a capital is the archaeologists' reading ('appears to have been the centre of a fairly extensive kingdom', Shu page).

correction.text: the culture's range, 'the Chengdu Plain', with the walled city at Guanghan, Deyang prefecture

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Sanxingdui row). The infobox gives c. 1700 to c. 1150 BC; the page lists the culture's range as the Chengdu Plain and gives no area for the culture, only 3.6 km2 for the walled city. The disc of 100 km round Chengdu is the researcher's stand-in; muted and dotted as a culture, never a state boundary.

region.text: the culture's range, 'the Chengdu Plain', with the walled city at Guanghan, Deyang prefecture

ledger.note: c. 1700 BC: the Sanxingdui culture on the Chengdu Plain. Infobox 'Dates: c. 1700 - c. 1150 BC'; Period I belongs to the Baodun culture and Periods II-III are the Sanxingdui culture, 'contemporaneous with the Shang dynasty'. Region is the researcher's reading of 'Chengdu Plain'.
c. 1600 BC: a walled city is founded at Sanxingdui. 'Archaeological digs at the site showed evidence of a walled city founded c. 1,600 BCE'; a trapezoid of about 3.6 km2 with walls 8-10 m high.

region.text: the culture's range, 'the Chengdu Plain', with the walled city at Guanghan, Deyang prefecture

ledger.note: c. 1150 BC: the Sanxingdui culture ends. The infobox ends it c. 1150 BC; the page dates no cause (flood, earthquake or invasion are suggested) and Jinsha, 40 km away, 'is thought to be the relocated capital of the Shu kingdom' (Jinsha page: Shi'erqiao culture 1200-800 BC).

certainty.note: An archaeological distribution, never a boundary; soft throughout.

sources.title: Sanxingdui
sources.note: Infobox c. 1700-c. 1150 BC; walled city c. 1600 BC of 3.6 km2; four phases; the Chengdu Plain; the Shu identification.

sources.title: Jinsha site
sources.note: The successor centre, 40 km from Sanxingdui (the Sanxingdui page), thought to be Shu's capital; 'Shi'erqiao culture 1200-800 BC'.

notes: Pages opened (2 of 1-2): Sanxingdui, Jinsha site. Wikidata id left null (unreachable). TYPE culture, though the schema's culture type is pre-3400 BCE: the Sanxingdui culture is a Bronze Age archaeological culture contemporary with the Shang; the Shu state starts at 1046 (the first dated mention) in the shu dossier and many archaeologists identify the two, so a gap-filler may prefer to merge them; the pages give a gap of about a century. The 'capital_move' event is the founding of the walled city (no earlier seat is on the page). The end date is the infobox's; the page gives 'c. 1150' without a cause. AREA: only the walled city's 3.6 km2; no culture area, no Cliopatria row.
